subject: Next steps: Apex Retail POC scope & API integration plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@apexretail.com>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@apexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC scope, success criteria, and API/SDK plan

Hi Emily / Carlos — thanks again for the demo call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a short POC for item-level recommendations in Apex’s product feed.

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: Improve search relevance and recommendation lift for product detail pages (especially long-tail SKUs).
- Success criteria (mutually agreed):
  - +8% CTR on recommended products for the seeded test set OR +6% uplift in add-to-cart for recommendations within 3 weeks of POC run.
  - Latency target: 95th percentile generation < 300ms for single-item queries.
  - Integration must not send PII; only product metadata and anonymized session ids.

Proposed POC scope (3-week focused run)
1) Week 0 (prep): security review, sample dataset, and access to their staging API.
2) Week 1: SDK integration into recommendation service + baseline logging.
3) Week 2: Run live A/B with Redwood route vs control, telemetry collection.
4) Week 3: Evaluation, metrics report, and rollout recommendations.

Key responsibilities
- Redwood (Dev / me): provide SDK example (Python + Node), streaming example for incremental context, sample integration code for tool-calling (e.g., external price-check service), test endpoints, and a lightweight evaluation script.
- Apex (Emily / Carlos): provide a sanitized sample feed (CSV/Parquet), staging credentials, and target metric tracking (CTR/ATC).
- Neha: program owner for POC logistics and billing.

Integration specifics (technical checklist)
- SDK: We will provide a scoped SDK package with a single-file example showing tokenized request, batching config, and error handling (redelivery/backoff).
- API routes: Recommend using the /v1/generate endpoint for candidate text generation and /v1/embeddings for similarity rerank. We will share concrete route examples and recommended model variants (quantized CPU fallback + GPU low-latency).
- Streaming: We'll include a streaming sample (server-sent events) so you can render progressive recommendations while the full rerank completes. Streaming will be optional for the POC but useful to test perceived latency.
- Tool calling: If you need tool-calling (price-check / inventory lookup), we support a simple webhook-style call pattern; Dev will include a pattern that shows how Redwood triggers a tool and returns structured tool outputs.

Attachments: I attached a short POC requirements spreadsheet to this thread with fields we need (dataset size, expected QPS, staging IPs).

Next steps / asks
- Emily: Can you confirm dataset availability (target: 10k product rows) and provide an indicative QPS?
- Carlos: Can you share the security questionnaire (if you have one) so we can loop in security?
- Neha: I’ll coordinate dates — proposed start May 25 if we get staging access this week.

If that aligns, Dev and I will prepare the SDK samples and a one-page runbook for the integration.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@apexretail.com>

Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@apexretail.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:07:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC scope, success criteria, and API/SDK plan

Thanks Vanessa — this is great and aligns with what the team heard. A few clarifications from our side: we can get you a sanitized product feed of ~12k rows and our staging service can handle up to ~15 QPS for the trial window.

Two asks from security/compliance:
1) We will send our security questionnaire (SOC2 items + network ACLs) — tagging Carlos.
2) For token handling, can you confirm session_id hashing is supported on your SDK examples so we never transmit raw session ids?

On tool calling: we want the pattern to hit an internal price-check microservice in our VPC. Is it possible to do the webhook-style tool call over a tunneled connection or do you recommend a callback pattern?

Proposed start date May 25 works for us as long as access is provided by end of week.

Appreciate the clear success criteria — we’ll confirm internally and get back by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Emily
